text:
ash: FYI I'm seeing a burst of DNS failures from GPU edge pods in us-west-2 and eu-central-1. Pods trying to hit internal .svc FQDNs are getting SERVFAIL or no response for ~5-12s, then succeed. Started right after an egress change. tagging infra oncall. :eyes:

deploy-bot: deploy event: egress config change applied by mike at 2026-03-18T07:58:47Z (commit d9f7b2c)

mike: that was the conntrack/source-port randomization tweak to spread SNAT ports under heavy batching. i changed the iptables SNAT rule to use more port ranges — rolling that back now.

ash: pasted /etc/resolv.conf from gpu-node-11 (redacted):
```
search svc.cluster.local cluster.local example.internal
nameserver 10.96.0.10
nameserver 10.200.42.5
options ndots:5 timeout:5 rotate
```
nslookup repeatedly shows: 
```
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
Server: 10.96.0.10
Address: 10.96.0.10#53

** server can't find model-registry.svc.cluster.local: SERVFAIL
```

talia: which node-local-dns version? and are we sending parallel queries to multiple forwarders? ndots:5 + rotate will cause fanout.

ash: node-local-dns v0.3.1 on those nodes. logs show a spike of upstream queries to 10.200.42.5 and intermittent SERVFAILs + short TCP timeouts (200-600ms). after a quick restart of the node-local-dns pod I saw the failures drop for ~7m then return.

jen: recall we bumped ndots to 5 in the kube-dns config to help tenant search paths. Combined with "rotate" and multiple forwarders that will parallelize queries and increase the packet rate toward each forwarder. If the forwarders apply per-src-port or per-src-IP rate limits, randomized SNAT ports can increase apparent concurrency and trip their defenses.

mike: rolling back SNAT port rollouts now 1: revert committed at 08:05 UTC. if that clears it's likely the changed SNAT distribution increased effective query rate to fragile forwarders.

ash: tried mitigation: 1) remove "rotate" from resolv config on a canary AZ so queries go to primary forwarder first, 2) restart node-local-dns daemonset on that AZ. After both the observed SERVFAILs dropped dramatically. putting this as P1->P2 for now.

talia: runbook snippets: 
```
# restart node-local-dns
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart ds/node-local-dns
# remove rotate: edit ConfigMap kube-dns -> stubDomains/upstreams/options and remove 'rotate' from options
```

mike: opened INC-12345 and assigned to eng-infra oncall. tagging networking team to coordinate with upstream forwarder owners to loosen rate-limits or pin per-AZ forwarders. https://redwood.incidents/INC-12345

jen: longer-term options we should discuss: [1] reduce ndots back to 2 for GPU-heavy pools, [2] enforce aggressive positive caching for cluster.local answers in node-local-dns, [3] pin a per-AZ preferred forwarder and avoid rotate for low-latency services, [4] talk to forwarder owners to raise rate limits or add burst allowance for our SNAT ranges.

ash: revert completed 08:11 UTC. will instrument upstream RTT, SERVFAIL counters, and per-node query rates. scheduling a short change window to stabilize resolver defaults.

mike: thumbs up. follow-up tasks: commit revert to infra repo, schedule ndots/rotate policy change for GPU node pools, and sync with forwarder owners. :thumbsup:

jen: noted in INC-12345, will add postmortem if recurrence within 48h. thanks team.
